prize_parts.citation: For developing the theory of firm heterogeneity and selection in international trade, showing how trade reallocates resources across firms and shapes aggregate productivity and the gains from trade.

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged in substance: B010, Melitz and Helpman, as a single achievement. My reasons are the common criteria and not support counts. Melitz (2003) is a precisely identifiable model of selection into exporting and of reallocation across firms. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, adds the exporting-versus-FDI choice, a distinct and well-documented second contribution. The framework is more than twenty years old and has been taken up in trade, macro, development and industrial organisation. A two-person credit line leaves no arbitrary cut among listed names. The chair's round-1 summary shows no position near six supporters, so I do not treat any current count as informative about merit. I did reconsider moving to B032. It is the candidate I find closest to B010 on merit, and I respect its design-based evidence on local adjustment, which is close to my own regional work. I stay with B010 for two reasons that apply to both candidates under the same standard. First, its credited unit is cleaner. B032 requires choosing between Dorn and Katz and leaves the task-theory credit partly outside the ballot. Second, the mechanism I would honour does not depend on a contested aggregate magnitude. What did change is my citation. After Fredriksson's round-1 point, I have narrowed it to the theoretical framework of selection and reallocation, with no claim to have discovered the exporter-premia facts and no welfare magnitude. My confidence is moderate. I would not defend this as clearly superior to B032 on science alone.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains attribution at the edges. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum developed closely related heterogeneous-firm ideas and the early empirical facts, and none of them is credited on this ballot. A Helpman-Melitz prize therefore cuts through a larger lineage, and the citation can only mitigate this. The second reservation is quantitative. Welfare gains from selection depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity, and sufficient-statistics results suggest the gains may be smaller than first claimed. Dreber Almenberg is right that this makes the model-based welfare claims less directly checkable than reduced-form local evidence. Third, Redding is excluded on my view that his quantitative and spatial work is a separable later strand. A member who sees it as part of one programme could reasonably disagree. Finally, I cannot independently verify priority questions or what the 2008 prize covered. These rest on my own recollection and on colleagues' accounts.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranks B010 first with Helpman and Melitz. He asks that the citation rest on the theoretical framework of firm heterogeneity and selection and its implications for gains from trade, and not claim discovery of exporter premia or firm-level stylised facts, because the Bernard et al. lineage is uncredited. He keeps B032 as an alternative and would lean to Autor and Hanson plus either Katz or Dorn.
responses.response: I accept his wording point and have revised my citation. It now credits the theory of firm heterogeneity and selection, with reallocation and aggregate productivity as consequences, and it does not mention exporter facts or a welfare magnitude. That is accurate to the credited names, and it is the only honest way to handle the uncredited lineage, since the Committee can credit only listed people. On B032 I share his view that the strand question has to be settled before the names. I would add that a citation for trade-shock evidence only points to Dorn, and I do not think Katz can be added without making the task-theory question unavoidable.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg ranks B032 first and ranks B010 below it because the firm-heterogeneity model's quantitative welfare gains depend more on functional form than transparent reduced-form designs do. She holds that the exposure designs have been re-examined with alternative inference and that the local effects have held up, while the aggregate magnitude has not.
responses.response: I accept the distinction in part. The size of the selection-based welfare gain is more assumption-dependent than the qualitative local effects in B032, and I have removed any magnitude from my citation for that reason. I would not extend the argument to the mechanism. Exporter selection and within-industry reallocation are predictions that firm-level data in many countries have tested, and the debate about welfare size is conducted in the framework's own terms. I cannot evaluate the latest shift-share inference literature myself, and I note that you and Teorell say your knowledge of it is incomplete. The chair asked what evidence supports calling B032 mature, and that gap leaves me unable to rank B032 above B010 on maturity grounds. I do not see a decisive scientific difference between them, only a difference in how cleanly the credit can be attributed.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B014 first with Calvo, Taylor and Woodford and ranks B010 second. He treats the three as separable building blocks, accepts that the cut leaves out Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, and says the Committee should be explicit about whether it honours theory or the estimation strand. He also warns that B010 may split trade support and that quantitative work suggests smaller selection gains.
responses.response: I agree that his trio is the most defensible three-person cut within B014 and that its maturity is not in question. The chair's question about substituting Galí or Gertler is for his side to answer, but I note that he concedes the estimation-strand decision is unresolved. That unresolved choice is the main reason I do not rank B014 first. Eight credited names and two distinct strands make any trio contestable in a way a two-person B010 is not. On B010 I accept the size-of-gains point and the risk of split trade support. I handle the first through citation wording and cannot resolve the second. If the Committee decided that the BEJK lineage disqualifies a Helpman-Melitz award, I would move to B032 before B014, because I find the B032 evidence base closer to my own criteria.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B032 first with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. She moved from Katz to Dorn because the local labour-market design is a joint Autor-Dorn-Hanson contribution, and she frames the citation around the China-shock evidence as the identified core, not the whole task theory. She acknowledges that task credit also lies outside the ballot.
responses.response: This is the strongest version of the B032 case, and I agree with her on the third name. If B032 is chosen, Dorn rather than Katz follows from a trade-shock citation, because Katz's skill-premium work is a separate earlier strand. Her narrowing of the citation addresses most of my attribution worry. The remaining difference between us is small. I prefer B010 because its credited unit needs no choice between two strands and no exclusion of a close co-originator. That is a judgement about cleanliness, not a claim that B032 is weaker science. I would regard a B032 award with her citation as defensible.

responses.point: Andersson now prefers B014 and lists B010 and B032 as alternatives. He regards B010 as the cleaner attribution and B032 as more policy-salient but more debated, and he places B014's attribution difficulty alongside Galí and Gertler's claims.
responses.response: I agree with his characterisation of B010 as the cleaner attribution and of B032 as more debated on magnitude. I would not treat policy salience as an advantage in a prize for scientific discovery, since breadth of influence on trade, macro and industrial organisation is what I weigh. I also note that he and I are Lund colleagues, which I disclose below, and that I did not rely on that tie. He and I agree that the citation should avoid empirical overclaiming. Where we differ is whether the B014 attribution problem can be resolved by choosing the originators. I think it can be managed but not removed, and I do not see it as cleanly resolved by any trio.

uncertainties: Whether the uncredited Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum lineage should be treated as disqualifying or as a gap a narrowly worded citation can manage. I cannot resolve this from the supplied materials.
How much the quantitative welfare-gains debate (Pareto assumption, sufficient-statistics results) should affect how the achievement is characterised, even with magnitudes removed from the citation.
Whether Redding belongs in the credit as part of one programme or is a separable later strand. I treat him as separable and a member who disagrees could reasonably differ.

Whether B032, with Autor, Dorn and Hanson and a trade-shock-only citation, is the better choice. I find it close, and I lack up-to-date knowledge of re-examinations of shift-share inference and persistence.
Whether the Committee views recognising trade in this year as compatible with competing trade candidates outside the shortlist. I have no evidence here to compare them.
Prior-prize facts (the 2008 and 2022 prizes, Gertler's status) are recollections stated by members and by me. None has been verified in this exercise.
statement.conflict_note: Updated, disclosed and not adjudicated. The supplied profile documents no co-authorship or institutional tie to Melitz, Helpman or Redding, nor to the B032 names (Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Katz) or the B042 names (Kiyotaki, Moore). My connections are to Lund colleagues, including committee member Tommy Andersson, who prefers B014 and lists B010 as an alternative, and to Johannes Lindvall, Alexandra Cermeño and the Lund economic-history school. None of these is credited on any ballot in my configuration or alternatives. My research on regional growth and local adjustment, including identification of local effects from infrastructure, is thematically adjacent to the China-shock literature in B032 and to Redding's spatial work. That is field proximity, and I applied the same criteria across fields. My 2023 presentation speech and 2025 press role do not establish a personal preference and were not used as evidence.
